title: Burnout Paradise by Ponycam at the Astor Place Theatre #burnoutparadi...
transcript: Four people on treadmills on stage performing a series of highly physical tasks — what could go wrong? In Burnout Paradise, the fringe hit by the collective Ponycam, a group of burnt out artists race against time to beat their distance record and complete a laundry list of assignments across four categories: survival, admin, performance, and leisure. If you're familiar with the Neofuturists, this show has a similar artistic sensibility, though it's arguably even more chaotic due to the number of things happening simultaneously. If audience participation is your thing, this show is a feast — there's actually no way that all the tasks can get done without an audience that's equally invested in completing them all on time. But even if going on stage to deliver a prop or collaborate on a task isn't your thing, I guarantee you will still be very engaged. You'll more likely than not be overstimulated, but in a good way. Burnout Paradise is running now at the Astor Place Theatre. With that, another program for my collection.
